title: Sync between devices
summary: A learner's phone and computer keep one set of data in step, directly over the local network.
description:
One learner, several devices. A device shows a QR code and another scans it; from then on the two form a vault and sync whenever both are open on the same Wi-Fi. There is no server and no account: devices talk to each other directly, encrypted, and only to devices that were paired.

Whole rows sync, not operations. Every device reaches the same result whatever order changes arrive in.

requirements.text: Two devices are paired by scanning a QR code that carries a one-time token valid for 10 minutes.
Joining a vault replaces the joining device's synced data with the vault's; a device holding data of its own says what it holds and asks first, and a backup is taken before it is replaced.
A local change is synced within a few seconds while a paired device is reachable, and a Sync now button syncs on demand.
On Android the app also syncs in the background about every 30 minutes, on unmetered networks only.
Coming back to the front asks for a sync and reloads what is on screen; a drill or check-in in progress keeps its own data.
A device can be removed from the vault; its key is revoked and it is refused from then on.
When two devices changed the same row without seeing each other, the later change wins, with ties settled by device id.
Append-only tables (the learning log, the mastery ledger, an answer's words) are written once by one device and never conflict.
A day's totals are kept per device and summed when read, so two devices practising on the same day do not overwrite each other.
Settings about the device stay on it: theme, time zone, reminders, audio prefetch, repeat mode, haptics, speaking cards and the marks that say built-in content was seeded.
Work in progress is carried on only by the device that started it: a song being made, a picture being drawn, a tutor reply being written.
A database put back from an older copy is noticed and takes a new device identity before it syncs.
Devices sync only when their schema versions are equal, and debug and release builds never sync with each other.
Connections are encrypted with Noise, and a peer whose key is not in the vault, or is revoked, is refused.
An interrupted sync resumes: changes are pulled in batches of at most 500 rows and about 4 MB, applied in small transactions, and the bookmark moves only with a batch's last part.
On a computer in a vault a snapshot of the database is kept daily: one a day for 7 days, then one a week up to 28 days.
Android's own backup is off, so a restored phone never carries another device's sync identity.
Every synced table's triggers list all of its columns; a test fails otherwise.
